description: Compound annual growth rate between a beginning and an ending value over a number of years: the constant yearly rate that turns one into the other, (ending / beginning)^(1 / years) - 1. A smoothed average: it hides the path and the volatility in between, and it says nothing about future growth. Both values must be positive. Edge cases: beginningValue and endingValue above zero (a start or end of zero or below has no growth rate); years above zero and at most 1000, a fraction of a year is fine. Not covered: contributions or withdrawals in between (that is not CAGR), the path and volatility between the two dates, and any forecast; CAGR smooths a bumpy path into one rate. Use when user asks "what is the CAGR of my portfolio?" or "what yearly growth takes $10,000 to $25,000 in 8 years?". Returns: cagr, totalReturn, growthMultiple, logGrowthRate (all fractions; logGrowthRate is the continuously compounded rate).

endingValue.description: Value at the end (positive), same currency

years.description: Years between them, above 0 and at most 1000 (fractions allowed, e.g. 2.5)
